e:
ERV = volume expired after a normal expiration down to maximal expiration.
FRC = ERV + RV (lungs' volume at end of normal expiration)

Heat stroke (>40°C): thermoregulation fails → classically anhidrosis, hot dry red skin.
Tachypnea & hypotension are seen; sweating is not

Inulin clearance = GFR, constant (filtered only).
PAH clearance (~RPF) is highest at low plasma levels & falls once secretory Tm is saturated.
Glucose/HCO₃⁻: fully reabsorbed (clearance ≈ 0) until their threshold is crossed

Refractory period = from threshold (start of depolarization) till end of repolarization.
Absolute RP: no stimulus works (Na⁺ channel inactivation); relative RP: stronger stimulus needed

Facilitated diffusion: via carrier/channel protein, down the gradient, no ATP, saturable (e.g., GLUT).
Simple diffusion needs no protein
Preterm RDS = ↓ surfactant → ↑ surface tension → alveolar collapse & ↓ compliance
↑ ECF K⁺ ↓es the K⁺ gradient → less K⁺ efflux → RMP becomes less negative (depolarized)

Lateral dorsal column = fasciculus cuneatus (upper limb) → ipsilateral arm proprioception lost.
Medial = fasciculus gracilis (lower limb)
Plateau (phase 2) = slow, prolonged L-type Ca²⁺ influx balancing K⁺ efflux → long refractory period
β2 → Gs protein → adenylyl cyclase ↑es cAMP → bronchial smooth muscle relaxation

SGLT1 = Na⁺–glucose cotransporter of the intestinal brush border (secondary active) → basis of ORS.
SGLT2 = renal PCT

Giant 'a' wave = right atrium contracting against a stenosed tricuspid valve.
TR → giant c-v wave instead

ICF: K⁺ (~140) is the main cation, very low Na⁺ & Cl⁻.
ECF: Na⁺ ~140, Cl⁻ ~100, K⁺ ~4
Stress incontinence: ↑ intra-abdominal pressure (cough/strain) overcomes a weak sphincter/pelvic floor → leakage c̅ no urge
Hyperventilation (resp. alkalosis) ↑es albumin-bound Ca → ↓ ionized Ca²⁺ → tetany, perioral numbness, seizures, laryngospasm

Thiazides ↑ Ca²⁺ reabsorption in the DCT → ↓ urinary Ca²⁺ → prevents Ca stones.
Loop diuretics do the opposite (↑ Ca excretion)

Optimal sarcomere length (~2.2 µm): maximal thick–thin overlap & cross-bridges → peak tension.
Too stretched or too short → ↓ tension

Kearns–Sayre = mitochondrial DNA deletion (maternal inheritance).
Williams = 7q deletion; achondroplasia = AD; CF = AR
High altitude → hypoxia → hyperventilation → ↓ PaCO₂ → respiratory alkalosis (renal HCO₃⁻ loss compensates later)

Net filtration = (Pc − Pi) − (πc − πi) = 0
(18 − Pi) − (27 − 7) = 0 → Pi = −2 mmHg
